title: RAPID: evaluation of Cas12a protospacer nicking and chimeric reporters for PAM-independent RNA and DNA diagnostics.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Fetched the Europe PMC full text and the article XML. The XML lists exactly one supplementary item: a single PDF, gkag748_supplemental_file.pdf (no spreadsheets, no CSV/TSV). The Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint returned HTTP 500 on one attempt and the NCBI open-access service returned 404 for PMC13434338, so no supplementary file could be opened. No accession in the text: text-mining found only ON563414 (a GenBank virus sequence) and 8Y03 (a protein structure), neither of which is this paper's measured data. Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI returned nothing.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All experiment counts come from the Methods and Results text: nicks at 24 positions on the target strand (Supplementary Table S1) plus a set of non-target-strand nicks (Table S2) and one extra nicked duplex (Table S3); 16 reporter chemistries screened; single/double mismatch panels in single-stranded DNA and microRNA; 25 nasopharyngeal patient samples (14 negative, 11 positive) compared with reverse-transcription quantitative PCR. The actual readout (plate-reader fluorescence over 5 hours, 3 technical replicates) appears only in figures; I could not confirm any numeric table exists.

a1_downloadable.note: No machine-readable data anywhere. The data availability statement says data are 'in the article and in its online Supplementary Material', with anything further 'from the lead contact upon request' and materials under a materials transfer agreement. The only supplementary item in the article XML is one PDF, and both Europe PMC (HTTP 500) and the NCBI open-access service (404) failed to serve it, so even the PDF was not retrievable here.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The label would be trans-cleavage activity (how fast Cas12a chews a reporter once activated). It is not a column anywhere: it exists as fluorescence-versus-time curves plotted in the paper's figures, so it would have to be reconstructed by digitising plots.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are oligonucleotide sequences (guide RNA, target strand, non-target strand, reporters) and are listed in Supplementary Tables S1-S3 of the PDF, so they are present as sequences rather than accessions - but only as PDF text that would need re-typing or parsing.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated in the Methods for the assay conditions (nanomolar enzyme, guide and reporter, millimolar magnesium, emission at 530 nm, readings once per minute for 5 hours); from the paper text only, since no data file was opened.

a5_enough_rows.note: The largest single experiment is 24 nick positions along the protospacer. Adding the non-target-strand nicks, 16 reporters, the mismatch panels and 25 patient samples still leaves well under 200 distinct measured conditions - far below the ~400 minimum for even a classification task. This is a hypothesis-driven assay-development paper, not a screen.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; size was never the problem.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all, because no data file was obtainable. The text itself is also inconsistent on the clinical cohort: the Results say 21 SARS-CoV-2 patient samples in one place and 25 nasopharyngeal samples (14 negative, 11 positive) in another.

a8_label_provenance.note: The readout is a direct physical measurement - fluorescence from a quencher-released reporter in a plate reader - not another model's output and not computable from the input sequences, so provenance is clean. It just is not available in numeric form.

existing_models.name: DeepCas12a (2026, BMC Genomics) - a convolutional network plus vision-transformer model predicting AsCas12a guide RNA cutting efficiency from the 34-base-pair target sequence plus DNA methylation and chromatin accessibility
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported average precision 0.783, area under the receiver-operating curve 0.868, Spearman correlation 0.630 on an independent test set (split definition not inspected by me).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: They argue activity is not set by local sequence alone but by global interactions across the guide-target duplex, which is why they added long-range attention.

existing_models.name: DeepCpf1 - the original convolutional network for Cas12a (Cpf1) guide activity, with a chromatin-accessibility-aware variant
existing_models.score_and_split: Widely used reference model for cis-cleavage guide efficiency; I did not retrieve its exact reported numbers, so none quoted.

existing_models.name: Guide-RNA design models for Cas12a diagnostics (e.g. the 2024 'Deep learning enhancing guide RNA design for CRISPR/Cas12a-based diagnostics' work, and a crRNA-DNA interaction-feature model built on a library of >23,000 feature sequences reporting Pearson correlation 0.93)
existing_models.score_and_split: Pearson correlation ~0.93 reported for the interaction-feature trans-cleavage model on its own library; split not inspected.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer or DNABERT-2 (DNA language models) would be the natural backbone for short protospacer/reporter sequences
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would be plenty for ~200 short sequences, but there is nothing to train on.
backbone.licence: Backbone licences are permissive/non-commercial depending on checkpoint; irrelevant here.

integration.partner_dataset: None that helps: the paper's measurements are not in a joinable form, and public Cas12a datasets (e.g. the Cas12a-variant activity profiling in human cells) measure genome editing efficiency, not the nick-position trans-cleavage effect measured here.
integration.join_key: none available (no identifiers; only free-text oligonucleotide names in a PDF)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written - with no shared key and no numeric labels, any join would be decoration.

controls.positive_control: In principle the known position-dependence of nicking (activity drops when the nick sits near the seed region) could serve as a control, but with ~24 points it is a figure, not a model test.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling would be meaningless at this sample size.
controls.external_validation: None: no second lab has published nick-position trans-cleavage series in numeric form that I found.

honest_claim_h3: Any model fitted to this paper would claim only 'on 24 nick positions in one protospacer measured in one lab, activity varies with position' - a description of a single figure, not a predictive claim.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use guide and target sequence plus nick position to predict how fast Cas12a cuts a reporter.
plain_idea.train_on: What I considered: each example would be one assay condition - the guide RNA sequence, the target sequence, where the single-strand break (nick) sits, and the reporter chemistry. Verified count of examples: about 24 nick positions in the main series, under ~200 conditions in the whole paper.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be trans-cleavage speed, i.e. how quickly the activated enzyme cuts a fluorescent reporter. The true answer comes from fluorescence read once a minute for 5 hours on a plate reader, in 3 technical replicates.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Diagnostics labs designing CRISPR-based tests would use a reliable activity predictor to skip rounds of trial-and-error reporter and guide design; but this paper does not supply enough measurements to build one.

more_or_better_data.why: Roughly 24 nick positions and 16 reporters here, versus published Cas12a activity models trained on thousands to tens of thousands of guide-target pairs (one reported library of over 23,000 feature sequences).

confidence_score.why: Three technical replicates per condition exist in principle, which would let you estimate noise, but the replicate values are not released in numeric form, so no calibration is possible.

models_beatable.why: The closest existing models are recent (DeepCas12a, 2026; guide-design models for Cas12a diagnostics, 2024) and report strong numbers; with ~200 conditions we could not train anything comparable, let alone beat them.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails on the first condition: our model cannot see everything the baseline sees, because this paper's measurements are not available as numbers, and the quantity measured (trans-cleavage on nicked activators) differs from the cis-cleavage editing efficiency the published models predict.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict Cas12a trans-cleavage activity from protospacer sequence, nick position and reporter chemistry. The biology is genuinely interesting (nicks tune activation in a position-dependent way, and RNA/chimeric reporters cut background), but the paper releases no numeric measurements - only a single supplementary PDF of oligonucleotide sequences plus figures - and the whole study comprises under ~200 assay conditions.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: a few hundred short DNA/RNA sequences embed in seconds on a laptop CPU. Compute was never the constraint; the absence of labels is.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the article XML and count supplementary items: one PDF, no tables. That alone kills it, and took one fetch.

verdict_reason: No machine-readable data (one supplementary PDF, rest 'upon request'), and only ~24 nick positions plus ~16 reporters measured - fails A1, A2, A5 and A7.
